_comment: POSIX filesystem and access control rules for Saffell-Soft. Consumed by rbac_fs.py and rbac_sync.py. Edit this file to change permissions — do not hardcode rules in the scripts.

_tier_model._comment: Declarative documentation of the permission inheritance hierarchy. rbac_fs.py and rbac_sync.py implement this via ACL entries — POSIX does not have native inheritance so each tier's access is explicitly granted on the relevant paths.

tiers.access: rw on own_paths + all Employee paths (inherited)
rw on own_paths + read Employee paths + read Manager paths (inherited)

flat_roles.access: read-only on manager/reports and /var/log only — no saffell-soft folder access beyond that

parent_dirs._comment: World-traversable. Manager and Board reach employee subfolders via ACL grants. Employee is blocked from manager/ and board/ at those parent dirs.
Manager group traverses freely. Board gets r-x via ACL. Employee blocked as others (mode 750). 3PAO gets r-x via ACL to reach manager/reports.
Board group traverses freely. All others blocked as others (mode 750).

folders._comment: Tier 1. Employee rw (group owner). Manager rw (tier 2 inherits). Board r (tier 3 inherits). Others: none.
Tier 1. Employee rw (group owner). Manager rw (tier 2 inherits). Board r (tier 3 inherits). Others: none.
Tier 2. Manager rw (group owner). Board r (tier 3 inherits). Employee: blocked. Others: none.
Tier 2. Manager rw (group owner). Board r (tier 3 inherits). 3PAO r (flat ACL). Employee: blocked. Others: none.
Tier 3. Board rw (group owner). Employee and Manager: blocked. Others: none.

acls._section: employee/ parent — audit marker only, subfolders enforce access

acls._comment: Employee rw + default so new files inherit group-write. Mask prevents stripping.
Tier 2 inherits Tier 1 — Manager rw on employee folders.
Tier 3 inherits Tier 1 — Board read-only on employee folders.
Tier 2 inherits Tier 1 — Manager rw on employee/projects.
Tier 3 inherits Tier 1 — Board read-only on employee/projects.

acls._section: manager/ parent — Board and 3PAO traversal grants, deny_manager audit marker
acls._comment: Board needs r-x on manager/ parent to traverse into subfolders (Tier 3 inherits Tier 2).
3PAO needs r-x on manager/ parent to reach manager/reports.
Audit marker for deny_manager — named-user denies applied by rbac_sync.py.
Manager rw + default. Mask prevents stripping.
Tier 3 inherits Tier 2 — Board read-only on manager/shared.
Belt-and-suspenders — Employee explicitly denied on manager/shared.
Manager rw + default. Mask prevents stripping.
Tier 3 inherits Tier 2 — Board read-only on manager/reports.
3PAO flat read on manager/reports — no inheritance, no write.
Belt-and-suspenders — Employee explicitly denied on manager/reports.
Board rw + default. Mask prevents stripping.
Belt-and-suspenders — Employee explicitly denied on board/workspace.

external_acls._comment: ACL entries on paths outside base_dir. Applied by rbac_fs.py separately from the main acls list. /var/log is managed by the OS — we only add read grants, never change ownership or mode.
external_acls._reason: 3PAO flat read on system logs for compliance assessment.

deny_groups._comment: Maps deny group names to the folder paths they block. rbac_sync.py resolves current members and applies named-user ACL deny entries (user:<uid>:---). Named-user entries are used because POSIX group deny ACLs cannot override a positive grant from another group the same user belongs to.

sudo_controls._comment: Sudo access policy. Enforced by rbac_sync.py via OS group membership removal, not sudoers drop-in files. !ALL drop-ins are ineffective against group-based grants.
